headline: Dry, sunny and warm through Friday, with gusty northeast winds peaking on Thanksgiving and highs in the lower to mid 80s for most coasts and valleys, while a big swell and exceptionally high tides flood parts of the coast Thursday morning; next week's one truly impactful storm, Tuesday night into Wednesday, could bring 1–3 inches of rain at the coast and 3–5 inches in the mountains.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Wednesday warmed 3 to 6 degrees across the area under sunny skies, with highs 4 to 8 degrees above normal, and tonight stays dry around Glendale and the LA basin as dry winds blowing out from the interior (offshore winds) keep strengthening. Gusts in most areas stay just below advisory levels, with isolated advisory-level gusts in the windiest spots; a Wind Advisory has been added for the Santa Lucia Mountains on the Central Coast through 9 AM Friday. Light turbulence and wind shear are possible near Burbank, Van Nuys and Camarillo from about 3 to 9 AM Thursday, while LAX should see only light north to northeast winds around 5 mph.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: The offshore push peaks on Thanksgiving, with a Wind Advisory from 6 AM to 2 PM Thursday for the central San Gabriel and Santa Susana Mountains. With high pressure building overhead, Thanksgiving and Friday bring highs in the lower to mid 80s across most coasts and valleys, including the Glendale area. Offshore winds weaken Friday and a light ocean breeze returns Saturday, dropping coast and valley temperatures 4 to 8 degrees, with little change farther inland.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Next week turns very active, but only the midweek storm looks truly impactful; a system Sunday night into Monday morning and another next Friday should be relatively mild. The Tuesday night–Wednesday storm looks like a quick but potent cold front with about 6 to 8 hours of rain plus strong, gusty winds, potentially bringing 1 to 3 inches at the coast and 3 to 5 inches in the mountains. Most of the rain currently looks to fall overnight Tuesday into early Wednesday morning, with some showers likely lingering into Wednesday afternoon; snow stays mostly above 8,000 feet, with possibly a few inches down to 7,000 feet, and residents in sensitive areas should follow this one closely.

coast: A large, long-period west swell peaks through Thursday morning and combines with exceptionally high tides to bring large surf and moderate to significant coastal flooding, worst at the morning high tide and in low-lying spots with no protection from the ocean. The highest surf and worst flooding are expected on the Central Coast from Point Conception northward, the Ventura County coast and far eastern parts of the southern Santa Barbara County coast, under Coastal Flood Warnings until noon Thursday and High Surf Warnings until 3 AM or noon Thursday, followed by High Surf Advisories into Saturday; other beaches, including LA County, see somewhat lesser but still concerning impacts under Coastal Flood Advisories until noon Thursday and High Surf Advisories through Thursday. Expect strong rip currents nearly everywhere, strong along-shore currents, sneaker waves, heavy shore break, coastal erosion and a higher risk of damage to coastal structures, making swimming dangerous. On the water, Small Craft Advisories for rough seas and strong winds run into Thursday (until 3 AM Friday for some waters), with offshore winds at advisory strength from Point Mugu to Santa Monica into Thursday night, east to northeast winds at times north of Point Sal through Friday morning, and large breaking waves near harbor entrances through Thursday that can capsize small boats; rough seas persist on the outer waters and north of Point Sal through Friday, conditions stay mostly calmer Friday night through Monday, then winds increase to advisory levels or higher Monday night ahead of the approaching strong storm.
watch_for: Coastal flooding and dangerous surf at Thursday morning's high tide, worst on the Central Coast and Ventura County coast
Gusty northeast winds Thanksgiving morning, with isolated advisory-level gusts possible outside the advisory areas
The Tuesday night–Wednesday storm: 1–3 inches at the coast, 3–5 in the mountains, and strong winds, especially for sensitive areas
confidence: Forecasters say the warm, dry Thanksgiving forecast is in good shape and have moderate to high confidence in the marine forecast, while the potent midweek storm is still days out, so its timing and rain amounts could change.
